domain_label: Sweater QC — The Thread-Checker Decomposition, Code-Back Loop & AI-Vision Frontier
purpose: A method for deciding what a micro acrylic/blend knitwear brand should actually build versus demand when the owner proposes a 'thread-checker' — a device that grades thread-to-thread, records the grade, and sends a code back to the supplier. It decomposes that single idea into four layers (L1 sense-yarn, L2 sense-knit, L3 grade, L4 code-back-to-the-named-spinner), shows that L1-L3 already exist as supplier-owned Uster-class capital plus pre-written USTER/ICI/AQL standards (so they are demanded in the purchase order, never built), isolates L4 (grade-then-code-to-the-named-spinner) as the one novel, ownable, near-free sliver (~$0-5k, a contract with a QR stamp, not a machine) whose leverage is conditional on a numeric PO spec, a willingness to reject, and an order big enough for the spinner to care; separates the buyer-to-supplier accountability loop from the consumer-facing digital-product-passport QR; sequences the moves NOW/LATER/NEVER; treats AI vision as the one brand-cheap frontier (software + camera) that must be validated on pre-production samples first and that assists, never replaces, the human inspector; and expresses every cost/price/throughput/MOQ figure as a labeled estimate, a cited fact, or an honest unknown that names a blocker rather than fabricating a number.
assumptions: the venture is a micro D2C acrylic/blend knitwear brand sourcing in Ludhiana and selling in California/Turlock, with a ~$1-2.50/garment yarn input inherited from the yarn deep-dive (T2)

the sensing-and-grading layers (L1 yarn evenness, L2 knit defects, L3 benchmark grading) already exist as supplier-owned six-figure capital and pre-written global standards, so they are demanded via the purchase order, not built

every cost, price, throughput, MOQ and accuracy figure is a labeled estimate (method + basis + confidence), a cited fact, or an honest unknown that names a blocker; cost/price/throughput/MOQ bands are estimates and never fake-precise
the L4 code-back loop is software glue on a contract (~$0-5k estimate, medium-high confidence): a scorecard plus a QR/grade stamp returned to the named spinner, not a machine

AI-vision defect-detection accuracy figures (91-96% / >95%) are reported on woven/jacquard datasets (e.g. TILDA) and do not transfer untested to our acrylic/blend stockinette and rib knits; accuracy on our fabrics is unknown until validated on pre-production samples
off-paper trade mechanisms in the Ludhiana cluster are described structurally as incentive, never as a named-party accusation, with magnitudes unknown
exclusions: the three-layer own/demand/buy QC posture and the incoming-AQL garment gate in full detail — covered by the QC-layers KB
the spinning-dial and contractual yarn-spec mechanics (CVm%, IPI, twist, hairiness, pilling-box thresholds) in full — covered by the QC-tech and yarn KBs
landed-cost, duty and unit-economics modelling that consumes the QC cost line — covered by the logistics/unit-economics KB
any claim that a home-built rig can credibly grade against USTER STATISTICS, or any promise of a magic device or a brand-built yarn-clearer/tester
consumer-facing brand storytelling and marketing execution for the digital-product-passport QR beyond distinguishing it from the supplier loop

competency_questions.question: What exactly is the owner's thread-checker idea, and why is decomposing it into four layers the move that resolves it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THREADCHECKER_FRAME states the idea (grade thread-to-thread, record, code back to supplier) and FOUR_LAYER_DECOMP splits it into L1 sense-yarn / L2 sense-knit / L3 grade / L4 code-back as the decomposition that gives each layer its own verdict

competency_questions.question: Why is L1 (sensing the yarn thread-to-thread) something to demand via the purchase order rather than build?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: L1_SENSE_YARN_EXISTS names USTER QUANTUM (in-line clearer, 100% thread-to-thread, logs every fault) and USTER TESTER 6 (off-line lab) as decades-deep supplier-owned six-figure capital versus a ~$1-2.50/garment input, concluding demand-not-build

competency_questions.question: What is the status of L2 (sensing knit defects) and L3 (grading), and why are neither built either?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: L2_SENSE_KNIT states auto fabric-inspection frames plus emerging vision exist (explore later, not build), and L3_GRADE_STANDARDS states USTER STATISTICS percentiles, ICI 1-5, the 4-point system and AQL are pre-written global standards to cite, never invent

competency_questions.question: Why is L4 (grade then code back to the named spinner) the one novel, ownable sliver, and what is it actually made of?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: L4_CODE_BACK_LOOP states nobody sells it turnkey because it is the brand's own contract instrument — a scorecard plus a QR/grade stamp returned to the named spinner, ~$0-5k estimate, a contract not a machine

competency_questions.question: What is the correct posture toward L1-L3, and how does the purchase order carry it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BUY_VIA_PO_POSTURE states the sensing-and-grading device the owner imagines already exists as supplier-owned benchmark-anchored capital, so it is demanded in the PO (or via a third-party lab cert for a micro-spinner who cannot self-test), never owned

competency_questions.question: What three conditions must hold for the L4 code-back loop to have any leverage, and which one is unknown?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the conditional leverage is stated as needing (1) a numeric PO spec to grade against, (2) a willingness to reject lots, and (3) an order big enough that the spinner cares — with the order-size condition flagged unknown

competency_questions.question: How is the buyer-to-supplier accountability loop different from the consumer-facing digital-product-passport QR, and why must they not be conflated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BUYER_SUPPLIER_LOOP_DISTINCT frames L4 as buyer-to-supplier accountability and CONSUMER_DPP_SEPARATE frames the EU-ESPR/TextileGenesis QR as a separate, forward-facing, later-if-marketing-wants-it consumer loop

competency_questions.question: Where does AI vision genuinely help, and where is it hype, for a brand-side QC budget?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AI_VISION_FRONTIER names it the one brand-cheap frontier (software + camera + lighting) for L2 knit-defect screening, while flagging that the cited accuracy numbers are dataset-specific and not the answer for yarn-evenness grading or final accept/reject

competency_questions.question: Why must any vision accuracy claim be validated on our own pre-production samples before it is believed, and what is the true cost of vision QC?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VISION_VALIDATION_GATE states the 91-96%/>95% figures come from woven/jacquard datasets (TILDA), that accuracy on our acrylic/blend knits is unknown, that PPS swatches must validate it first, and that the true cost is the labelled dataset not the camera

competency_questions.question: Even where vision works, what is its correct role relative to the human inspector?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VISION_ASSISTS_NOT_REPLACES states vision is a screening/triage layer that assists the human linker/inspector, never the final accept/reject authority for a small premium line

competency_questions.question: How is QC cost-per-lot and expected defect-escape traded against spec rigor, and how is that relationship recomputed when inputs change?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QC_COST_DEFECT_FORMULA recomputes a labeled cost-per-lot (lab spot-check + inspector man-day + amortized L4 loop) and an expected-defect-escape that falls as spec rigor and sampling rise, with every dollar input tagged estimate or unknown and refreshed on a real quote

competency_questions.question: What is the cheapest-first NOW / LATER / NEVER sequence of QC moves for this brand?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEQUENCE_NOW_LATER_NEVER places the numeric PO + demanded cert + incoming AQL + per-lot lab spot-check + the L4 loop in NOW, a validated vision/used inspection rig in LATER, and owning a Tester 6 / building a clearer or the sensing thread-checker in NEVER

competency_questions.question: What is the bottom-line verdict on the thread-checker, and how is every money/accuracy claim kept honest?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THREADCHECKER_VERDICT delivers build-only-the-cheap-L4-loop / don't-build-the-sensor, and HONESTY_GUARDRAIL enforces FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tagging, no over-promising, and off-paper-as-mechanism-not-accusation across every claim

competency_questions.question: How is the thread-checker decision refreshed when a blocking unknown closes or an input changes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THREADCHECKER_REVIEW_LOOP defines a cadence and material-change triggers (a vision-accuracy validation result, a real per-lot lab/inspection quote, a spinner actually acting on a returned code, a DPP regulatory date) that re-run the formula, the conditional-leverage read and the verdict

glossary.definition: The owner's proposed device that grades yarn (and knit) thread-to-thread, records the grade, and sends a code back to the supplier; resolved here by decomposing it into four layers whose verdicts differ — the sensing/grading layers are demanded via the PO and only the code-back loop is built.

Splitting the thread-checker into L1 sense-yarn (read evenness/faults along the thread), L2 sense-knit (read defects in the knitted panel), L3 grade (turn readings into a benchmark-anchored verdict) and L4 code-back (return a grade/scorecard per lot to the named spinner); L1-L3 already exist, L4 is the ownable sliver.

The one novel, ownable piece: log each lot's grade to a scorecard and emit a grade code / QR back to the named spinner; software glue on a contract, an estimated ~$0-5k, a contract with a QR stamp rather than a machine.

The on-winder yarn clearer that checks yarn thread-to-thread, 100% in-line, records and cuts/re-splices every fault and logs to the cloud — literally 'grade every bit of thread and record it', already productised and living on the spinner's machine (a fact, Uster Technologies).

The off-line lab evenness tester (capacitive + optical) measuring CVm%, IPI, hairiness, count-CV and tenacity graded against USTER STATISTICS; six-figure-USD class, exact list price unknown (Uster does not publish), reconciled band ~$80k-400k+ (estimate, low confidence) — never owned by a micro-brand.

The posture toward L1-L3: the sensing-and-grading device the owner imagines already exists as supplier-owned, benchmark-anchored, six-figure capital, so the brand specifies the number in the purchase order and makes the spinner prove it — or pays a third-party lab where a micro-spinner cannot self-test — and never owns the instrument.

The L4 loop has teeth only if three conditions hold: a numeric PO spec exists to grade against, the brand will actually reject lots, and the order is big enough that the spinner cares — the third condition flagged unknown, since a micro-capsule's returned code may simply be ignored.

Two distinct QR loops kept separate: the L4 buyer-to-supplier accountability loop ('here is your grade on this lot') versus the consumer-facing brand-to-consumer digital product passport (EU ESPR basic ~2027 / full ~2028-29; TextileGenesis), which is a separate, forward-facing, later-if-marketing-wants-it option.

The rule that any AI-vision defect-detection accuracy claim (91-96% / >95% on woven/jacquard datasets such as TILDA) is treated as marketing until validated on our own acrylic/blend pre-production samples; accuracy on our knits is unknown and the true cost is the labelled defect dataset, not the camera.

Even where AI vision works, it is a screening/triage layer that flags candidate defects for the human linker/inspector, never the final accept/reject authority for a small premium line, and never the answer for yarn-evenness grading (Uster does that better and benchmark-anchored).

A labeled estimate of the fraction of defective garments that pass the QC gate and reach the customer; it falls as spec rigor (a numeric PO + post-wash pilling gate) and AQL sampling rise, and is traded against QC cost-per-lot in the formula node.

source_registry.description: labeled estimates, cited standards and honest unknowns for the thread-checker decision of a micro Ludhiana-sourcing knitwear brand, grounded in the quality-checker deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md), its reconciled brief, the yarn deep-dive (~$1-2.50/garment input and the contractual-QC posture), and the shared scope glossary; the sensing/grading layers are anchored to published Uster Technologies methodology and ISO/AQL standards, the cost bands to triangulated public reportage tagged estimate, and the AI-vision accuracy claims to their dataset-specific published origins
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Uster Technologies USTER STATISTICS methodology and USTER TESTER 6 / USTER QUANTUM (4.0) clearer datasheets (uster.com; Textile World 2021); ISO 12945-1 (ICI Pilling Box, grade 1-5); ISO 2859-1 / ANSI-ASQ Z1.4 (AQL sampling; apparel defaults Critical 0 / Major 2.5 / Minor 4.0; QIMA/ASQ); 4-point fabric-inspection system; TILDA fabric-defect dataset and published CV knit-defect-detection papers (91-96% / >95% on woven/jacquard); EU ESPR Digital Product Passport timeline (basic ~2027, full ~2028-29) and TextileGenesis traceability; third-party textile-lab cost norms (compliancegate / India textile-lab reportage, estimate); sweater-vertical SCOPE_GLOSSARY.md, quality_checker DEEPDIVE.md and reconciled.md, yarn DEEPDIVE.md

nodes.definition: Frame the owner's proposal precisely: a device that grades yarn (and knit) thread-to-thread, records the grade, and sends a code back to the supplier. The instinct is correct and partly already shipping, so the resolving move is not yes/no but decomposition — the single idea is really four different things with opposite verdicts, and confusing them is the expensive mistake. This node fixes the idea and motivates splitting it before any build/buy call is made.

included: the precise statement of the idea
why decomposition (not a single verdict) is the move
the framing that the instinct is correct but conflated

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the owner restates or expands the thread-checker idea

pros.claim: Stating the idea precisely and committing to decompose it prevents a premature single yes/no on a conflated proposal
pros.example: treating 'thread-checker' as one device leads to either building a six-figure sensor or dismissing a good instinct; decomposition avoids both

cons.claim: Decomposition can feel like deflecting the owner's idea rather than answering it
cons.example: an owner wanting a yes may read four layers as bureaucratic hedging

failure_modes: answering the idea as a single build/buy decision
dismissing the instinct as naive instead of decomposing it
acceptance_tests: the idea is stated as grade-thread-to-thread + record + code-back-to-supplier, and the need to decompose it into layers before verdict is made explicit
revisit_triggers: the owner restates or expands the idea
a new layer of the proposal is articulated

nodes.definition: Decompose the thread-checker into four layers, each with its own build/demand verdict: L1 sense-yarn (read evenness and point-faults along the thread), L2 sense-knit (read defects in the knitted panel), L3 grade (turn readings into a benchmark-anchored verdict), and L4 code-back (return a grade/scorecard per lot to the named spinner). The headline result the rest of the KB proves: L1-L3 already exist (Uster capital plus pre-written standards) so they are demanded, not built, and only L4 is the novel, ownable sliver.

included: the four named layers L1/L2/L3/L4
the headline split (L1-L3 demand, L4 build)
the opposite-verdicts framing
excluded: the per-layer evidence (each layer's own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a layer's existence or boundary status changes

pros.claim: Naming four layers turns one ambiguous idea into four answerable questions with separable verdicts
pros.example: L1 'don't build, demand' and L4 'build cheaply' coexist only once the layers are separated

cons.claim: A four-way split can over-formalize what an owner sees as one device
cons.example: the L2/L3 boundary blurs when a vision system both senses and grades a knit defect

failure_modes: collapsing L2 and L3 so a vision demo is mistaken for credible grading
treating all four layers with a single verdict
acceptance_tests: all four layers (L1 sense-yarn, L2 sense-knit, L3 grade, L4 code-back) are named and the L1-L3-demand / L4-build headline is stated
revisit_triggers: a layer's existence status changes (e.g. an L4 product appears)
the L2/L3 boundary needs re-drawing for a new vision tool

nodes.definition: Establish that L1 — sensing the yarn thread-to-thread — already exists as supplier-owned capital and must be demanded, not built. USTER QUANTUM (the in-line clearer on the spinner's winder) checks yarn thread-to-thread, 100% in-line, records every fault, cuts and re-splices, and logs to the cloud — literally the owner's 'grade every bit and record it', already productised [FACT, uster.com]. USTER TESTER 6 is the off-line lab counterpart measuring CVm%, IPI, hairiness, count-CV and tenacity against USTER STATISTICS. Both are six-figure capital (Tester 6 reconciled band ~$80k-400k+ [ESTIMATE, LOW]) against a ~$1-2.50/garment input; a home-built rig can demo a reading but cannot credibly grade against the benchmark — that is Uster's moat. Verdict: demand it via the PO; never own it.

included: USTER QUANTUM in-line clearer and TESTER 6 lab
the six-figure-vs-$1-2.50/garment disproportion
the demand-not-build verdict for L1

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a real Uster instrument price or a credible low-cost sensor appears

pros.claim: Showing the exact product that already does L1 settles the build question with a cited instrument, not an opinion
pros.example: USTER QUANTUM logging every thread-fault inline is the owner's idea already shipping on the spinner's machine

cons.claim: The exact tester price stays an unknown, so the own-vs-rent math cannot be closed precisely
cons.example: the ~$80k-400k+ band is a wide low-confidence estimate, not a quote

failure_modes: believing a home-built rig can credibly grade against USTER STATISTICS
treating the unknown exact price as a reason to reconsider owning
acceptance_tests: USTER QUANTUM (in-line, thread-to-thread, logs faults) and TESTER 6 (lab) are named as supplier-owned six-figure capital, tagged FACT for existence and ESTIMATE-LOW for price, with the demand-not-build verdict stated
revisit_triggers: Uster publishes or a quote reveals a real tester/clearer price
a credibly benchmark-anchored low-cost yarn sensor appears on the market

nodes.definition: Establish the status of L2 — sensing defects in the knitted panel. It partly exists as automatic fabric-inspection frames (used-rig entry ~$3k → knit-specialised ~$82k+ [ESTIMATE/listings, MED]) and emerging camera-vision. Unlike L1 it is not a deep metrology moat, but the brand-side vision option is unvalidated on our fabrics (see the vision nodes), so the verdict is explore later, not build now — and certainly not build a bespoke sensing device. L2 is where the AI-vision frontier lives, which is why it gets a conditional 'later' rather than L1's flat 'never own'.

included: auto fabric-inspection frames and emerging vision as the L2 sensors
the explore-later (not build) verdict
the link to the vision frontier
excluded: the vision validation gate detail (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an L2 rig/vision price or a volume trigger changes

pros.claim: Separating L2 from L1 captures that knit-defect sensing is cheaper and less moated, so it earns a 'later' not a 'never'
pros.example: a used inspection frame at ~$3k entry is a different economic question than a six-figure yarn tester

cons.claim: An 'explore later' verdict can drift into never if no volume trigger is ever set
cons.example: without a proven-repeat-volume trigger, L2 exploration is deferred indefinitely

failure_modes: building a bespoke knit-sensing device instead of buying a frame or validating vision
treating the ~$3k-$82k+ rig band as a precise capex line
acceptance_tests: L2 is stated as partly-existing (auto inspection frames + emerging vision), tagged ESTIMATE for the rig cost band, with the explore-later-not-build verdict and the pointer to the vision frontier
revisit_triggers: a style reaches proven repeat volume justifying an L2 rig
a knit-specialised inspection rig or vision tool drops materially in price

nodes.definition: Establish that L3 — grading — is a set of pre-written global standards to cite, never to invent. USTER STATISTICS percentiles (e.g. 25% USTER = better than 75% of world production) grade yarn evenness; the ICI Pilling Box scale 1-5 (ISO 12945-1) grades pilling; the 4-point system grades fabric defects; AQL (ISO 2859-1 / ANSI-ASQ Z1.4) grades lots accept/reject. A DIY grade has no credibility because the scales are the credibility — the percentile benchmark is Uster's whole moat. Verdict: cite the standard, do not build a grading engine.

included: USTER STATISTICS percentiles, ICI 1-5, 4-point, AQL as the L3 standards
the cite-not-invent verdict
why a DIY grade lacks credibility
excluded: the numeric PO spec values (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a grading standard is revised or a gap appears

pros.claim: Anchoring L3 to named global standards removes any temptation to build a non-credible in-house grade
pros.example: '25% USTER on CV% and IPI' is a citeable benchmark a spinner already understands; a home grade is not

cons.claim: Relying on external standards means the brand cannot grade on a parameter no standard covers
cons.example: a brand-specific defect with no published scale has no benchmark to cite

failure_modes: inventing a DIY grading scale that no supplier recognizes
quoting a percentile or pilling grade without naming its standard
acceptance_tests: USTER STATISTICS percentiles, ICI 1-5 (ISO 12945-1), 4-point and AQL are named as the pre-written L3 standards with the cite-not-invent verdict, tagged FACT for the standards
revisit_triggers: a relevant standard is revised
a brand-relevant parameter emerges with no existing published scale

nodes.definition: State the posture that follows for L1-L3: the sensing-and-grading device the owner imagines already exists as supplier-owned, benchmark-anchored, six-figure capital, so the brand's QC starts as a number in the purchase order and the spinner is made to prove it — handing over a USTER certificate (or, where a Ludhiana micro-spinner cannot self-test [ESTIMATE, MED-HIGH], a third-party lab cert the brand pays for). The reframe: you do not build the part that senses and grades; you demand it. This posture is the spine on which the L4 loop and the formula's defect-escape both rest.

included: the demand-via-PO posture for the sensing/grading layers
the supplier-cert vs third-party-lab-cert fork for micro-spinners
QC-starts-as-a-PO-number reframe
excluded: the full numeric PO clause content (numeric-spec node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: spinner self-test capability or a lab-cert cost is confirmed

pros.claim: Locating QC in the PO makes the highest-leverage QC nearly free and keeps six-figure capital off the brand's books
pros.example: writing '25% USTER on CVm% and IPI' costs only precision yet shifts the metrology burden to the spinner

cons.claim: A micro-spinner who cannot self-test forces the brand to fund a lab cert, eroding the free-QC claim
cons.example: if the chosen spinner owns no tester, the cert becomes a paid third-party lab line the brand carries

failure_modes: assuming any spinner can hand over a USTER cert when micro-spinners often cannot self-test
owning an instrument the PO posture says to demand
acceptance_tests: the demand-via-PO posture is stated for L1-L3 with the supplier-cert-or-paid-lab fork and the QC-starts-in-the-PO reframe, tagged ESTIMATE-MED-HIGH for the micro-spinner-cannot-self-test claim
revisit_triggers: the chosen spinner's self-test capability is confirmed

nodes.definition: Establish L4 — code back to the named spinner — as the one novel, ownable piece. Log each lot's grade to a scorecard and emit a grade code / QR back to the named spinner ('here is how lot #47 scored on CVm%, IPI, pilling'). Nobody sells this turnkey because it is the brand's own contract instrument, not a machine: a spreadsheet/app plus a QR stamp, an estimated ~$0-5k [ESTIMATE, MED-HIGH]. It is worth building because it is nearly free and is a real negotiation/selection instrument — over a few lots the brand sees which spinners are chronically out-of-spec, then re-prices or drops them. The reframe: the thread-checker is the part you already buy (sensing+grading via the PO) plus this cheap part you bolt on.

included: the scorecard + grade-code/QR-to-named-spinner mechanism
the ~$0-5k contract-not-machine framing
its use as a spinner-selection/negotiation instrument
excluded: the three leverage conditions (their own nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a turnkey code-back product or a real build cost appears

pros.claim: Building only the code-back loop captures the genuinely novel sliver at near-zero cost
pros.example: a QR scorecard returned per lot turns scattered cert numbers into a spinner-performance record for re-pricing

cons.claim: A cheap loop can be mistaken for a product when its value is entirely contractual and conditional
cons.example: building the app without a numeric PO behind it produces a code-back with nothing credible to grade

failure_modes: scope-creeping the loop into a bespoke sensing device
shipping the loop with no numeric PO spec behind the grade it returns
acceptance_tests: L4 is stated as a scorecard plus grade-code/QR returned to the named spinner, tagged ESTIMATE-MED-HIGH at ~$0-5k, framed as a contract instrument not a machine, with its spinner-selection use named
revisit_triggers: a turnkey code-back product appears on the market
the build estimate is replaced by a real implementation cost

nodes.definition: State the first condition for the L4 loop to have teeth: a numeric PO spec must exist to grade against. The code-back is empty unless the purchase order already carries the numbers — CVm% and IPI at a stated USTER percentile (25% USTER on mainstream acrylic/blend, never 5%), a hairiness ceiling, minimum tenacity, count plus count-CV tolerance, blend ratio with tolerance, and an ICI pilling acceptance (grade >=3-4 after a home wash). Without these numbers there is nothing to score lot #47 against, and the returned code is noise. This node is the spec spine the loop and the defect-escape both consume.

included: the numeric parameters the PO must carry to enable grading
the 25%-not-5% USTER mainstream target
the loop-is-empty-without-numbers point
excluded: the reject and order-size conditions (their own nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a PO spec parameter or target tier changes

pros.claim: Requiring numbers before the loop ensures the code-back grades against something credible
pros.example: scoring a lot against '25% USTER on CVm%+IPI, ICI >=3-4 post-wash' yields an actionable verdict; scoring against adjectives does not

cons.claim: Over-tight numeric targets can price out or alienate a flexible micro-spinner
cons.example: demanding 5% USTER on a mass acrylic lot is unquotable or luxury-priced and needlessly so

failure_modes: running the L4 loop with no numeric spec so the returned grade is meaningless
demanding luxury-tier percentiles on a mainstream lot
acceptance_tests: the numeric PO parameters (CVm%/IPI at 25% USTER, hairiness ceiling, tenacity min, count-CV, blend tolerance, ICI >=3-4 post-wash) are named as the precondition the loop grades against, with 25%-not-5% stated
revisit_triggers: a target tier proves wrong at sampling
a parameter is added to or dropped from the PO spec

nodes.definition: State the second condition: the loop has teeth only if the brand will actually reject lots. The numbers in the PO and the grade in the code-back are theatre unless a failing lot is genuinely refused or re-priced. AQL gives the statistical accept/reject rule (Critical 0 / Major 2.5 / Minor 4.0 apparel defaults), but the rule is inert without the operational and commercial willingness to send a batch back. This node is the behavioral condition that converts a measured grade into leverage.

included: the willingness-to-reject condition
the AQL accept/reject defaults as the rule it activates
QC-without-rejection-is-theatre
excluded: the AQL sampling mechanics in full (QC-layers KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a reject decision is actually made or forgone

pros.claim: Naming reject-willingness as a condition stops the loop being measurement theatre
pros.example: a Major-2.5 AQL failure only has teeth if the brand actually returns the batch rather than accepting it under deadline

cons.claim: A micro-brand under a launch deadline may be unable to afford to reject a marginal lot
cons.example: rejecting the only available lot before a drop can be costlier than accepting a minor defect rate

failure_modes: specifying numbers and a code-back but never enforcing a rejection
treating AQL as documentation rather than a live accept/reject gate
acceptance_tests: the willingness-to-reject condition is stated as the behavioral activator of the AQL accept/reject rule, with QC-without-rejection-is-theatre made explicit
revisit_triggers: a lot fails and the reject decision is actually tested
a deadline forces an accept-the-defect trade-off

nodes.definition: State the third and weakest condition: the loop has leverage only if the order is big enough that the spinner cares — and whether that holds for a micro-capsule is UNKNOWN [Open-Q]. A returned grade code from a tiny buyer may simply be ignored; the spinner-selection power of L4 depends on the brand being a customer worth keeping in spec for. This is the binding uncertainty on the whole L4 value claim, named as a blocker, never fabricated: do spinners actually act on a returned code at our order size? Unknown until the relationship is real.

included: the order-must-be-big-enough condition
the UNKNOWN flag and named blocker
the micro-capsule-code-may-be-ignored risk
excluded: the numeric spec and reject conditions (their own nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a spinner is observed acting or not acting on a returned code

pros.claim: Flagging order size as an unknown keeps the L4 value claim honest rather than over-promised
pros.example: marking 'a tiny capsule's code may be ignored' as UNKNOWN prevents claiming guaranteed leverage

cons.claim: An unknown this central makes the L4 value contingent and hard to bank on
cons.example: the loop's main benefit cannot be guaranteed until a spinner is observed acting on a returned code

failure_modes: claiming guaranteed L4 leverage at micro-capsule volume
fabricating a threshold order size at which spinners start to care
acceptance_tests: the order-size condition is stated as the third leverage requirement and explicitly flagged UNKNOWN as a named blocker, with the micro-capsule-ignored risk noted and no fabricated threshold
revisit_triggers: a spinner is observed acting (or not) on a returned grade code
order volume crosses a level where the relationship changes

nodes.definition: Fix the identity of the L4 loop as buyer-to-supplier accountability: it points from the brand back to the named spinner ('here is your grade on this lot') and exists to select and discipline suppliers. This direction is what makes it a contract instrument rather than a marketing asset, and is the reason it lives on a numeric PO and a reject decision. Naming the direction explicitly prevents it being confused with the opposite-facing consumer loop, and frames why its leverage is conditional on the supplier relationship rather than on a consumer.

included: the buyer-to-supplier direction of the loop
why that direction makes it a contract instrument
the contrast hook to the consumer loop
excluded: the consumer DPP detail (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a proposal to merge supplier and consumer loops appears

pros.claim: Stating the loop's direction keeps it a supplier-discipline tool and not a mis-scoped consumer feature
pros.example: 'grade back to the spinner' is a sourcing decision; a customer-facing tag is a marketing decision — different budgets and owners

cons.claim: Insisting on the direction can seem pedantic when a single QR could in principle serve both ends
cons.example: a brand might wish one QR to both discipline the spinner and reassure the consumer, blurring the line

failure_modes: building the loop to face the consumer instead of the supplier
merging supplier-grade and consumer-passport data into one mis-scoped artifact
acceptance_tests: the L4 loop is stated as buyer-to-supplier accountability, with that direction explained as what makes it a contract instrument and distinct from the consumer loop
revisit_triggers: a proposal to merge the supplier and consumer QR loops arises
the loop's intended audience is questioned

nodes.definition: Distinguish the consumer-facing digital product passport from the L4 loop. Brand-to-consumer traceability QR (TextileGenesis-class; EU ESPR DPP basic ~2027 / full ~2028-29 [FACT, regulatory trend]) is a separate, forward-facing, later-if-marketing-or-regulation-requires-it option — not the supplier-accountability loop. Conflating the two mis-scopes both: the supplier loop is built now and cheaply for sourcing leverage, while the consumer passport is a future regulatory/marketing artifact with its own timeline and audience. Keep them on separate tracks.

included: the consumer DPP (ESPR timeline, TextileGenesis) as a separate loop
its later/forward-facing/optional status
the don't-conflate rule
excluded: consumer marketing execution of the passport

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the ESPR DPP timeline or a marketing decision changes

pros.claim: Separating the consumer DPP keeps the cheap supplier loop from being delayed by a future regulatory artifact
pros.example: the L4 loop ships now while the ESPR DPP waits on a ~2027-29 timeline and a marketing decision

cons.claim: Treating the DPP as purely 'later' risks under-preparing if regulation lands sooner than expected
cons.example: an accelerated ESPR timeline could make the consumer passport a near-term compliance need

failure_modes: delaying the cheap supplier loop until the consumer DPP is ready
ignoring the ESPR timeline until it becomes an urgent compliance gap
acceptance_tests: the consumer DPP is named with its ESPR ~2027 / ~2028-29 timeline as a separate, later, forward-facing loop, tagged FACT for the regulatory trend, with the don't-conflate rule stated
revisit_triggers: the ESPR DPP timeline or scope is updated

nodes.definition: Establish AI vision as the one brand-cheap QC frontier: it is software + a camera + lighting, not heavy iron, and it targets L2 — flagging holes, dropped stitches and streaks on a knitted panel from a camera feed, with consistency (a camera does not tire at hour 8) as the real value. This is the single layer where a brand can plausibly own a cheap capability, which is why L2 earned a 'later' not a 'never'. But it is a frontier, not a settled tool: it is not the answer for yarn-evenness grading (Uster does that better and benchmark-anchored) nor for final garment accept/reject, and its accuracy must be proven (next nodes).

included: vision as cheap software+camera L2 screening
consistency as its real value
where it is NOT the answer (yarn grading, final accept/reject)
excluded: the validation gate and dataset cost (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a vision tool's capability, price or scope changes

pros.claim: Naming vision the one brand-cheap frontier locates the single layer a brand can own without heavy capital
pros.example: a camera flagging dropped stitches on a panel is cheap hardware, unlike a six-figure yarn tester

cons.claim: Calling it a frontier can read as endorsement before accuracy is proven on our fabrics
cons.example: an owner could buy a vision rig on the 'frontier' framing before validating it

failure_modes: applying vision to yarn-evenness grading where Uster is better
treating vision as final accept/reject authority
acceptance_tests: vision is stated as the cheap software+camera L2 frontier with consistency as its value, and explicitly ruled out for yarn-evenness grading and final accept/reject
revisit_triggers: a vision tool's capability or price changes materially
a new defect class becomes camera-detectable

nodes.definition: Enforce the binding caveat on AI vision: the accuracy numbers quoted (91-96% / >95% defect detection) come from specific datasets (TILDA; woven and jacquard fabrics) [FACT that they are reported], NOT from our acrylic/blend stockinette and rib knits — loop texture, fabric stretch, barre, and heather/melange colour noise are real confounders, so accuracy on OUR fabrics is UNKNOWN. Treat any '~95%' claim as marketing until validated on our own pre-production samples (PPS swatches from T8 sampling) [ESTIMATE-HIGH that it does not transfer untested]. And the true cost of vision QC is the data, not the camera — building a labelled dataset of OUR defects and validating a model is the expensive part, its cost and lead-time for a micro-brand UNKNOWN [Open-Q]. This is the single make-or-break input for any brand-side vision or thread-checker claim.

included: the dataset-transfer caveat (woven/jacquard not our knits)
validate-on-PPS-first rule
the data-not-the-camera cost and its UNKNOWN

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a vision accuracy is measured on our fabrics or a dataset cost is quoted

pros.claim: Holding the accuracy claim UNKNOWN until PPS validation prevents buying a vision rig on transferred numbers
pros.example: a >95% TILDA figure tells us nothing about barre and melange noise on our acrylic rib until tested

cons.claim: Demanding PPS validation adds a sampling cost and delay before any vision benefit
cons.example: building a labelled defect dataset of our knits is a real, UNKNOWN-cost prerequisite

failure_modes: believing a vendor/paper accuracy figure without validating on our fabrics
treating the camera as the cost while ignoring the labelled-dataset cost
acceptance_tests: the 91-96%/>95% figures are tagged FACT-as-reported and dataset-specific (woven/jacquard/TILDA), accuracy on our knits is flagged UNKNOWN, PPS validation is required first, and the data-not-camera cost is named as an UNKNOWN blocker
revisit_triggers: a vision model is validated on our PPS swatches with a measured accuracy
a labelled-defect-dataset cost/lead-time is quoted

nodes.definition: Fix the role of AI vision even where it works: it is a screening/triage layer that flags candidate defects for the human linker/inspector, never the final accept/reject authority for a small premium line. A skilled human reading seam/linking quality and shade is still the standard; vision is a multiplier on that human (catching what tiredness misses), not a substitute. No magic device, no brand-built machine — vision ASSISTS, it does not replace. This guards against the over-promise that a camera could run the QC gate unattended.

included: vision as screening/triage for the human
human as final accept/reject authority
the assists-not-replaces / no-magic-device guard
excluded: the incoming-AQL human gate in full (QC-layers KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: validated vision accuracy changes the human's role

pros.claim: Casting vision as an assistant preserves the human accept/reject standard a premium line needs
pros.example: vision triages panels at speed while the linker still makes the final seam/shade call

cons.claim: An assist-only role caps the labour savings a brand might hope vision delivers
cons.example: if vision cannot replace the inspector, the headcount saving is screening-time only, not the whole gate

failure_modes: promising an unattended vision QC gate
removing the human accept/reject authority on a premium line
acceptance_tests: vision is stated as a screening/triage assistant with the human as final accept/reject authority, and the no-magic-device/assists-not-replaces guard is explicit
revisit_triggers: vision accuracy on our fabrics reaches a level that changes the human's role
the premium-line accept/reject standard is reconsidered

nodes.definition: Recompute, as a labeled estimate, the QC cost-per-lot and the expected defect-escape as a function of spec rigor, and trade them off. QC_cost_per_lot = lab_spot_check_cost (~$30-250/lot [ESTIMATE, MED]; a discrete per-sample Uster run near Ludhiana UNKNOWN) + inspector_man_day_rate x days (~$100-350/day [ESTIMATE, MED]) + amortized_L4_loop (~$0-5k [ESTIMATE, MED-HIGH] spread over lots) + amortized_vision (only if validated, else 0). Expected_defect_escape = base_escape x (1 - sampling_coverage) x (1 - spec_rigor_factor), where spec_rigor_factor rises with a numeric PO and an ICI >=3-4 post-wash gate and sampling_coverage rises with the AQL plan; escape falls as rigor and coverage rise, while cost rises with more tests, tighter sampling and the amortized loop/vision. Every dollar input is tagged ESTIMATE or UNKNOWN; the node recomputes whenever a quote replaces an estimate, and feeds the brand's recurring QC cost line (to T4) and the verdict.

included: the cost-per-lot sum (lab + inspector + amortized loop + amortized vision)
the defect-escape-vs-rigor relationship
the estimate/unknown tagging of every input
excluded: the spinning-dial derivation of the spec (yarn KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a QC cost input is quoted or an amortization basis changes

pros.claim: A recomputing formula turns the rigor-vs-cost trade into an auditable, estimate-tagged number instead of a vibe
pros.example: raising AQL coverage and adding a post-wash pilling test lowers expected escape while pushing cost-per-lot up a known, labeled increment

cons.claim: With several UNKNOWN inputs the formula outputs a wide band, not a point
cons.example: an UNKNOWN per-sample Uster run and an estimate inspector rate keep cost-per-lot a range until quoted

failure_modes: presenting the formula output as a precise figure rather than an estimate band
fabricating an UNKNOWN input (e.g. a per-piece job-work rate) to make the number look precise
acceptance_tests: cost-per-lot is computed as lab (~$30-250) + inspector (~$100-350/day) + amortized L4 (~$0-5k) + amortized vision, each tagged ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN, and expected-defect-escape is shown falling as spec rigor and AQL coverage rise; the node recomputes when an input changes
revisit_triggers: a real per-lot lab or inspection quote replaces an estimate
a per-sample Uster run cost near Ludhiana is quoted
the L4 or vision amortization basis changes

nodes.definition: Sequence the QC moves cheapest-first. NOW (~$0 capital): write the numeric PO spec, demand the spinner's USTER cert (or a paid third-party lab cert for a micro-spinner), AQL-sample incoming garments against a written standard (Critical 0 / Major 2.5 / Minor 4.0), buy a per-lot third-party lab spot-check (~$30-250/lot) for pilling/shrinkage/fastness/composition/evenness, and log every lot to a scorecard that emits a grade code/QR back to the named spinner (the L4 loop, ~$0-5k). LATER, only at proven repeat volume on a style: a used auto fabric-inspection rig (~$3k entry → $82k+ knit-specialised [ESTIMATE/listings, MED]) or a vision screening layer — but only AFTER PPS validation. NEVER: own a USTER Tester 6, build a yarn clearer, or build the sensing-and-grading thread-checker device — disproportionate to a ~$1-2.50/garment input and reinventing a metrology moat.

included: the NOW / LATER / NEVER cheapest-first ordering
what falls in each bucket
the proven-volume and PPS-validation gates on LATER
excluded: the final build/buy verdict (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a volume trigger fires or a NOW move completes

pros.claim: A cheapest-first sequence prevents capital being spent before the near-free moves are exhausted
pros.example: the numeric PO and L4 loop ship before any inspection rig or vision spend is even considered

cons.claim: A fixed sequence can defer a genuinely worthwhile LATER move if the volume trigger is set too high
cons.example: a style that repeats fast might justify a vision layer sooner than a conservative trigger allows

failure_modes: spending on a LATER rig before the NOW moves are in place
moving a NEVER item (Tester 6, built clearer) into scope
acceptance_tests: the NOW (numeric PO + cert + AQL + lab spot-check + L4 loop), LATER (validated vision / used rig at proven volume) and NEVER (own Tester 6 / build clearer or sensing thread-checker) buckets are each populated with their gates and cost tags
revisit_triggers: a style reaches proven repeat volume
a NOW move is completed and the next move is due

nodes.definition: Deliver the bottom-line verdict composing every layer: build ONLY the cheap L4 grade-code-back-to-the-named-spinner loop (~$0-5k), on top of a numeric PO spec and a real willingness to reject; do NOT build the sensing-and-grading device (L1-L3) — it is premature, reinvents Uster's metrology moat, and is disproportionate to a ~$1-2.50/garment input. The thread-checker is a contract with a QR stamp, not a machine: the part you already buy (sensing+grading via the PO) plus the cheap part you bolt on (the code-back loop). Its leverage is conditional, not guaranteed — it may be ignored at micro-capsule volume [UNKNOWN]. AI vision is the lone brand-cheap frontier but unproven on our knits and assists rather than replaces the inspector.

included: build-L4-only / don't-build-the-sensor verdict
the contract-with-a-QR-stamp framing
the conditional-leverage and vision caveats restated

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a leverage condition or vision validation resolves

pros.claim: A single composed verdict gives an actionable build/don't-build call instead of scattered layer reads
pros.example: the verdict says build the ~$0-5k loop and never the six-figure sensor, with leverage flagged conditional

cons.claim: Compressing four layers into one verdict can hide the conditions that qualify it
cons.example: a reader could take 'build the loop' as unconditional and skip the numeric-PO and reject preconditions

failure_modes: reading 'build the loop' as unconditional and dropping the preconditions
letting the verdict drift toward building the sensor under owner pressure
acceptance_tests: the verdict states build-only-the-L4-loop (~$0-5k) on a numeric PO + reject willingness, don't-build the L1-L3 sensor, frames it as a contract-not-a-machine, and restates the conditional-leverage UNKNOWN and the vision assists/unproven caveats
revisit_triggers: a leverage condition resolves (e.g. a spinner acts on a code)
vision is validated on our fabrics
the owner re-pushes to build the sensor

nodes.definition: Enforce the binding honesty discipline across every claim in this KB: money/capacity/performance/regulation claims are tagged [FACT] (public source), [ESTIMATE] (method + basis + confidence, literal word 'estimate'), or [UNKNOWN]. Cost/price/throughput/MOQ bands are ESTIMATEs and never fake-precise; a genuinely missing number (e.g. a Ludhiana per-piece job-work rate, a per-sample Uster run cost, the labelled-dataset cost) stays UNKNOWN and is named as a blocker, never fabricated. No over-promising: no magic device, no brand-built machine, and AI is a multiplier not a substitute. Off-paper cluster economy is described as mechanism, never as a named-party accusation, with amounts UNKNOWN. Coverage is a floor, not a ceiling. This guardrail governs how every other node may be expressed.

included: the FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tagging rule
no-over-promise and AI-as-multiplier
off-paper-as-mechanism-not-accusation and coverage-is-a-floor

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new claim is introduced or an UNKNOWN closes

pros.claim: A single guardrail keeps every money/accuracy claim honest and auditable
pros.example: tagging the ~$30-250/lot lab cost ESTIMATE and the per-sample Uster run UNKNOWN stops either being read as a quoted fact

cons.claim: Heavy tagging can make the analysis read as hedged and lower its perceived decisiveness
cons.example: a reader wanting one cost number is frustrated by an ESTIMATE band plus an UNKNOWN

failure_modes: letting a cost band be quoted as fake-precise
fabricating a missing number instead of naming it UNKNOWN
stating off-paper behavior as a named-party accusation
acceptance_tests: every money/capacity/performance/regulation claim is FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN-tagged, no missing number is fabricated, no over-promise (magic device/built machine) appears, AI is framed as multiplier, and off-paper is mechanism-not-accusation
revisit_triggers: a new node introduces a money/accuracy claim
an UNKNOWN closes with a real source
a public source is added or updated

nodes.definition: Define the loop that keeps the thread-checker decision current. A refresh cadence (re-run on each material data release) plus blocker-close triggers — a vision-accuracy validation result on our PPS swatches, a real per-lot lab or AQL inspection-man-day quote near Ludhiana, a per-sample Uster run cost, an observed instance of a spinner actually acting (or not) on a returned grade code, a labelled-defect-dataset cost/lead-time, or an ESPR DPP timeline update — that send the analysis back through the cost/defect formula, the conditional-leverage read, and the verdict. Without this loop the snapshot silently goes stale as the UNKNOWNs that gate the L4 value and the vision claim remain open. Each fired trigger replaces an ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN with a measured figure and re-runs only the affected nodes.

included: the refresh cadence
the blocker-close trigger list
re-entry into the formula, leverage read and verdict

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a blocker-close trigger fires or the cadence is tuned

pros.claim: A trigger list tied to the open UNKNOWNs keeps the lowest-confidence inputs on a path to resolution
pros.example: the first observed spinner response to a returned code fires the loop and upgrades the order-size-leverage UNKNOWN

cons.claim: Too-frequent refresh churns the decision when most inputs only resolve on the ground
cons.example: re-running the verdict before any quote or validation lands wastes effort

failure_modes: no cadence so the snapshot ages while its UNKNOWNs stay open
ignoring a fired trigger (e.g. a validation result) and continuing on stale estimates
acceptance_tests: a refresh cadence and a blocker-close trigger list (vision validation, lab/inspection/Uster quote, spinner-acts-on-code, dataset cost, ESPR update) exist, each routing back to the formula, leverage read and verdict
revisit_triggers: a blocker-close trigger fires
the cadence proves too frequent or too sparse for how the inputs actually resolve

conflict_axes.name: build_the_sensor_vs_demand_via_po
conflict_axes.description: The owner's instinct to build a thread-to-thread sensor pulls against the reality that L1-L3 already exist as supplier-owned capital to demand, not build.
poles: demand it via the purchase order
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: demand L1-L3 via the PO (or a paid lab cert); build only the L4 code-back loop; a home rig can demo but cannot credibly grade against USTER STATISTICS

conflict_axes.name: loop_value_vs_conditional_leverage
conflict_axes.description: The L4 loop is nearly free and attractive, yet its leverage is conditional on a numeric PO, a reject willingness, and an order big enough to matter — the last unknown.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: build the cheap loop but hold its leverage conditional; the order-size condition stays UNKNOWN until a spinner is seen acting on a returned code

conflict_axes.name: supplier_loop_vs_consumer_dpp
conflict_axes.description: The buyer-to-supplier accountability QR and the consumer-facing digital product passport tempt a single shared QR but serve opposite audiences and timelines.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep them separate: the supplier loop is built now for sourcing leverage; the consumer DPP is a later regulatory/marketing artifact (ESPR ~2027-29)

conflict_axes.name: vision_promise_vs_unvalidated_on_our_knits
conflict_axes.description: AI vision is the one brand-cheap frontier, but the quoted accuracy comes from woven/jacquard datasets and is unproven on our acrylic/blend knits.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat any ~95% claim as marketing until validated on our PPS swatches; the true cost is the labelled dataset, not the camera

conflict_axes.name: vision_replaces_vs_assists_inspector
conflict_axes.description: Hope that a camera could run the QC gate unattended pulls against the standard that a human reads seam/linking quality and shade on a premium line.
poles: keep the human as final authority
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: vision screens and triages; the human makes the final accept/reject; AI is a multiplier, not a substitute, and there is no magic device

conflict_axes.name: spec_rigor_vs_qc_cost
conflict_axes.description: More spec rigor and tighter sampling lower expected defect-escape but raise QC cost-per-lot, and the right point is a trade not a maximum.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set rigor where the marginal escape-reduction justifies the marginal cost; recompute as estimates harden into quotes

conflict_axes.name: cheap_now_vs_capital_later
conflict_axes.description: Near-free NOW moves compete with capital LATER moves (inspection rig, vision) whose timing depends on proven volume and validation.
poles: spend on a capital rig now
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: do the NOW moves first; gate any LATER capital on proven repeat volume and (for vision) PPS validation; never move a NEVER item into scope

conflict_axes.name: labeled_estimate_vs_decisiveness
conflict_axes.description: Rigorous FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tagging protects honesty but can make the cost and accuracy reads feel too hedged to act on.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: label every figure with a confidence and a blocker-close path so the read stays actionable without fabricating precision

conflict_axes.name: snapshot_stability_vs_open_unknowns
conflict_axes.description: The verdict reads as settled, but the order-size leverage and the vision accuracy are open UNKNOWNs that can move it.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the verdict as a dated baseline and let the review loop, not assumption, decide when a closed blocker has moved it

workflow.description: Name L1 sense-yarn, L2 sense-knit, L3 grade, L4 code-back with the L1-L3-demand / L4-build headline
workflow.gate: all four layers are named with their headline verdict split

workflow.description: Show L1 (and via siblings L2/L3) already exist as supplier capital and pre-written standards
workflow.gate: USTER QUANTUM/TESTER 6, inspection frames and the grading standards are named with demand-not-build verdicts

workflow.description: Place QC in the purchase order with the supplier-cert-or-paid-lab fork
workflow.gate: the demand-via-PO posture and the micro-spinner lab-cert fork are stated

workflow.action: Specify the numeric PO and the reject decision
workflow.description: List the numeric thresholds the loop grades against and the willingness to reject that activates them
workflow.gate: the numeric parameters (25% USTER, ICI >=3-4 post-wash, etc.) and the reject willingness are stated

workflow.action: Build the L4 code-back loop and its conditions
workflow.description: Define the scorecard + grade-code/QR loop and its three leverage conditions including the order-size UNKNOWN
workflow.gate: the loop is a ~$0-5k contract-not-machine with the three conditions and the order-size UNKNOWN named

workflow.description: Separate the buyer-to-supplier loop from the consumer ESPR/TextileGenesis passport
workflow.gate: the two loops are kept on separate tracks with the ESPR timeline stated

workflow.action: Assess the AI-vision frontier and gate it
workflow.description: Frame vision as the cheap L2 frontier, hold its accuracy UNKNOWN until PPS-validated, and keep it assistive
workflow.gate: the accuracy is flagged dataset-specific/UNKNOWN, PPS validation required, and the data-not-camera cost named

workflow.description: Compute cost-per-lot and expected defect-escape vs spec rigor with every input tagged estimate/unknown
workflow.gate: cost-per-lot sums labeled inputs and escape falls as rigor/coverage rise, recomputing on input change

workflow.description: Order the moves cheapest-first with the proven-volume and PPS-validation gates
workflow.gate: the NOW/LATER/NEVER buckets are populated with their gates and cost tags

workflow.description: Deliver build-only-the-L4-loop / don't-build-the-sensor with the conditional and vision caveats
workflow.gate: the verdict states the build/don't-build call and restates the conditional-leverage and vision caveats

workflow.action: Set the honesty discipline and the refresh loop
workflow.description: Apply FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tagging and define the blocker-close triggers that re-run the decision
workflow.gate: tagging is enforced and a blocker-close trigger list routes back to the formula, leverage read and verdict

priority_rationale: The frame and the four-layer decomposition are foundational because every verdict reads from them; the existing-capital layers (L1 yarn, L2 knit, L3 grade) and the demand-via-PO posture precede the L4 loop they make ownable; the numeric PO spec, reject willingness and order-size condition gate the loop's leverage; the buyer-to-supplier vs consumer-DPP distinction keeps the loop correctly scoped; the AI-vision frontier, its validation gate and its assist-only role govern the one brand-cheap frontier; the cost/defect formula trades spec rigor against QC cost and feeds the sequence; the NOW/LATER/NEVER sequence and the build/don't-build verdict compose all upstream reads; and the honesty guardrail plus the review loop come last because they govern how every claim is expressed and re-run the decision when a blocking unknown closes.

dominance_rules.rule: The demand-via-PO posture dominates any urge to build the sensing-and-grading device
dominance_rules.rationale: L1-L3 already exist as supplier-owned six-figure capital and pre-written standards a home rig cannot credibly match
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposal to build a thread-to-thread sensor or a DIY grading engine
dominance_rules.action: demand it in the PO (or a paid lab cert) and build only the L4 loop

dominance_rules.rule: A numeric PO spec dominates the L4 loop's existence
dominance_rules.rationale: a code-back grade is noise unless there is a numeric threshold to score against
dominance_rules.trigger: the L4 loop is built or run without numeric PO thresholds
dominance_rules.action: block the loop until the numeric spec (25% USTER, ICI >=3-4 post-wash, etc.) is in the PO

dominance_rules.rule: PPS validation dominates any vision accuracy claim
dominance_rules.rationale: cited 91-96%/>95% figures are woven/jacquard dataset-specific and do not transfer to our knits
dominance_rules.trigger: a vision tool is credited or bought on transferred accuracy
dominance_rules.action: treat the claim as marketing until validated on our PPS swatches and price the labelled-dataset cost

dominance_rules.rule: The human inspector dominates vision as the final accept/reject authority
dominance_rules.rationale: a premium line still needs a human reading seam/linking quality and shade
dominance_rules.trigger: vision is positioned to run the gate unattended
dominance_rules.action: keep vision as a screening assistant; the human makes the final call; AI is a multiplier not a substitute

dominance_rules.rule: The conditional-leverage flag dominates any claim of guaranteed L4 power
dominance_rules.rationale: the loop's leverage depends on order size, which is unknown for a micro-capsule
dominance_rules.trigger: the returned code is assumed to discipline the spinner regardless of order size
dominance_rules.action: mark the order-size condition UNKNOWN until a spinner is observed acting on a returned code

dominance_rules.rule: The honesty guardrail dominates any pressure for a single fake-precise number
dominance_rules.rationale: no QC cost or accuracy figure here is a measured fact, and a missing number must not be invented
dominance_rules.trigger: a request for a precise cost/accuracy or a missing per-piece rate
dominance_rules.action: give a labeled ESTIMATE band with confidence, or keep it UNKNOWN and name it as a blocker

dominance_rules.rule: The cheapest-first sequence dominates any early capital spend
dominance_rules.rationale: near-free moves must be exhausted before an inspection rig or vision is bought
dominance_rules.trigger: a capital QC rig is proposed before the NOW moves are in place
dominance_rules.action: complete the NOW moves and gate any LATER capital on proven volume and PPS validation

dominance_rules.rule: A closed blocker dominates the standing verdict
dominance_rules.rationale: a verdict built on UNKNOWNs must move when one resolves
dominance_rules.trigger: a vision validation result or a spinner-acts-on-code observation lands
dominance_rules.action: fire the review loop, replace the estimate/unknown, and re-run the affected formula, leverage read and verdict

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decompose the idea into the four layers before issuing any build/buy verdict
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a single yes/no on the conflated thread-checker that must be unpicked layer by layer later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Put the numeric PO spec in place before building the L4 loop
anti_rework_rules.prevents: shipping a code-back loop with nothing credible to grade, forcing a rebuild around the spec

anti_rework_rules.rule: Flag the order-size leverage UNKNOWN the first time the loop's value is claimed
anti_rework_rules.prevents: every downstream value claim inheriting an unflagged guaranteed-leverage assumption that must be re-marked

anti_rework_rules.rule: Hold vision accuracy UNKNOWN until PPS-validated and price the dataset, not the camera
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a vision purchase justified on transferred accuracy that a later validation contradicts

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep the buyer-to-supplier loop and the consumer DPP separate from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a merged QR artifact that must be re-scoped when the audiences and timelines diverge

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every cost/accuracy figure ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN at the moment it is written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later honesty sweep that must re-caveat figures already quoted as facts

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name each missing number as a blocker instead of fabricating it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a model built on an invented per-piece or per-sample figure that collapses when the real quote lands

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do the NOW moves before pricing any LATER capital rig or vision
anti_rework_rules.prevents: capex committed before the near-free moves prove the gap, then stranded when they suffice

iteration_protocol.trigger: a vision model is validated (or fails) on our acrylic/blend PPS swatches with a measured accuracy
iteration_protocol.action: replace the vision accuracy UNKNOWN, update its formula cost term and its LATER/NEVER placement, and re-run the verdict

iteration_protocol.trigger: a spinner is observed acting (or not) on a returned grade code at our order size
iteration_protocol.action: upgrade the order-size-leverage UNKNOWN and re-run the conditional-leverage read and the verdict

iteration_protocol.trigger: a real per-lot third-party lab or AQL inspection-man-day quote near Ludhiana lands
iteration_protocol.action: replace the lab/inspector cost estimates with measured figures and recompute cost-per-lot

iteration_protocol.trigger: a discrete per-sample Uster evenness run cost near Ludhiana is quoted
iteration_protocol.action: close that UNKNOWN in the formula and re-check the demand-via-PO economics

iteration_protocol.trigger: the chosen spinner's USTER self-test capability is confirmed or refuted
iteration_protocol.action: switch the cert source between supplier-cert and paid-lab-cert and update the cost line

iteration_protocol.trigger: a labelled-defect-dataset cost/lead-time for our knits is quoted
iteration_protocol.action: price the true cost of vision QC and re-evaluate the LATER vision move

iteration_protocol.trigger: the EU ESPR digital-product-passport timeline or scope is updated
iteration_protocol.action: re-date the consumer DPP track and confirm it stays separate from the supplier loop

iteration_protocol.trigger: a style reaches proven repeat volume justifying an L2 inspection rig
iteration_protocol.action: re-evaluate the LATER bucket and the rig cost term in the formula
